draft.title: Hypothetical Batching Throughput Tradeoff: Batch Size 1 vs. 4
draft.body: This post explores a hypothetical scenario regarding inference throughput when varying batch sizes for local LLMs. The experimental setup is purely illustrative and not based on actual measurements. In this hypothetical test, a batch size of 1 yielded a total throughput of 22 tokens per second. Increasing the batch size to 4 hypothetically resulted in a higher aggregate throughput of 55 tokens per second. It is crucial to note that these figures represent aggregate, not per-user, rates. Per-request latency was not a measured metric in this hypothetical exploration. These values are intended solely to illustrate a potential tradeoff and should not be interpreted as real-world performance data. Further discussion on how batching impacts perceived responsiveness versus raw throughput in practical local LLM deployments would be welcome.

draft.title: Illustrative Throughput Gains: Batching Size 4 vs. Batch Size 1 (Hypothetical)
draft.body: Exploring a hypothetical inference performance characteristic: the impact of batch size on aggregate token generation rate. For the purpose of this discussion, we consider an illustrative scenario where a batch size of 1 achieved a total output of 22 tokens per second. When the hypothetical batch size was increased to 4, the total throughput rose to 55 tokens per second. These figures are presented as aggregate rates, meaning they reflect the total processing capacity rather than individual request speeds. It's important to emphasize that per-request latency was not assessed in this hypothetical case. These numbers are purely for conceptual illustration and do not represent actual benchmark results. The core observation is the hypothetical increase in total output with larger batching, though this often comes with latency considerations not explored here.
